facts.fact_text: The youth group Committee for Protection of Rights of Young Political Prisoners (Gənc Siyasi Məhbusların Hüquqlarını Müdafiə Komitəsi) decided to hold a demonstration at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011 at the Seaside Boulevard in Baku.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants of the demonstration on 22 May 2011 were a group of ten to twelve persons.
The applicants attended the demonstration on 22 May 2011 at the Seaside Boulevard in Baku.
Shortly after the demonstration on 22 May 2011 had begun, the police started to disperse it.
According to the applicants, police officers followed and caught the applicants after they attempted to run away from the demonstration.
All three applicants were arrested by police officers V.I. and R.G. at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011.
Between 6.15 p.m. and 6.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011, administrative-offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued by police officer T.R. in respect of all three applicants.

The administrative-offence reports stated that at 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011, by deliberately failing to comply with the lawful order of the police, the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 310 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
Subsequently, police officer T.R. prepared administrative-arrest reports (inzibati qaydada tutma haqqında protokol) with respect to the first and second applicants.

According to the administrative-arrest reports, copies of which were submitted to the Court by the Government, the first applicant had been subjected to administrative arrest at 7 p.m. on 22 May 2011.

According to the administrative-arrest reports, copies of which were submitted to the Court by the Government, the second applicant had been subjected to administrative arrest at 7 p.m. on 22 May 2011.
The Sabail District Court convicted the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, to seven days' administrative detention.
The Sabail District Court convicted the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, to eight days' administrative detention.
The Sabail District Court convicted the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Sabail District Court sentenced the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, to seven days' administrative detention.
The Committee for Protection of Rights of Young Political Prisoners did not notify their plan to hold a demonstration to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority.

Police officers V.I. and R.G. submitted a report (raport) to a superior police officer stating that at around 5.30 p.m. at the Seaside Boulevard a group of young persons attempted to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out loud and disturbed people.
Police officers V.I. and R.G. stated in their report that when they wanted to calm down those persons, the persons ignored them.

The administrative-offence reports stated that at 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011, by deliberately failing to comply with the lawful order of the police, the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 310 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Police officer R.G. testified at the hearing of the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, that at around 5.30 p.m. on 22 May 2011 a group of persons attempted to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out loud and disturbed people.
Police officer R.G. testified that when he and his colleague wanted to calm down those persons, among them the first applicant Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, they disobeyed a lawful police order.

The statement that police officer R.G. gave against the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, was similar to his statement against the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, at the Sabail District Court hearing.

The statement that police officer R.G. gave against the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, was similar to his statement against the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, at the Sabail District Court hearing.
Police officer R.G. confirmed at the hearing of the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, that Mr Jamil Hajiyev had tried to escape by taxi and that the police officers had stopped that taxi.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstration on 22 May 2011 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants of the demonstration on 22 May 2011 were a group of ten to twelve persons.
The participants of the demonstration on 22 May 2011 were demanding the release of young persons arrested during some previous demonstrations.
According to the applicants, as soon as they noticed the police approaching they attempted to run away and leave the place of the demonstration.
According to the applicants, police officers followed and caught the applicants after they attempted to run away from the demonstration.

Police officers V.I. and R.G. submitted a report (raport) to a superior police officer stating that at around 5.30 p.m. at the Seaside Boulevard a group of young persons attempted to hold an unauthorised demonstration by shouting out loud and disturbed people.
Police officers V.I. and R.G. stated in their report that when they wanted to calm down those persons, the persons ignored them.
The Sabail District Court found that the first applicant, Mr Agasif Ibrahimov, had failed to stop participating in the unauthorised demonstration.
The Sabail District Court found that the second applicant, Mr Emin Farhadi, had failed to stop participating in the unauthorised demonstration.
The Sabail District Court found that the third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, had failed to stop participating in the unauthorised demonstration.
The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, stated before the Sabail District Court that he and other participants had been holding photos of arrested young persons without uttering any slogans.
The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, stated before the Sabail District Court that he had run away as soon as he saw the police approaching and had boarded a taxi.
The third applicant, Mr Jamil Hajiyev, stated before the Sabail District Court that police officers had stopped the taxi he had boarded and had forced him out.

The Report CommDH(2013)14 noted that the most frequent problems encountered included the banning of demonstrations in central and easily accessible locations and the use of force to disperse demonstrations, leading to arrests and in some cases harsh sentences.

Commissioner Nils Muižnieks noted that while the Law on Freedom of Assembly is in line with international standards, undue restrictions of the right to freedom of peaceful assembly are widely reported in practice.
Peaceful protesters have been effectively banned from demonstrating in central Baku since 2006, despite advanced notification of the assemblies.

Commissioner Nils Muižnieks stated that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

The Human Rights Watch Report (2013) stated that the Azerbaijani authorities have broken up unsanctioned demonstrations, often with violence, and have arrested and imprisoned peaceful protestors, organizers, and participants.

The Human Rights Watch Report (2013) stated that municipal authorities have effectively banned all forms of peaceful protest from the center of Baku and instead force all demonstrations into designated zones on the outskirts of the city.
The Human Rights Watch Report (2013) stated that for several years police have dispersed, at times violently, peaceful protests in Baku's center.
